title: Negation exchanges the two quantifiers
statement: Over any domain and any predicate P: not (for all x, P(x)) is equivalent to (there exists x with not P(x)), and not (there exists x with P(x)) is equivalent to (for all x, not P(x)).

formal.statement: (assert (and (= (not (forall ((x U)) (P x))) (exists ((x U)) (not (P x)))) (= (not (exists ((x U)) (P x))) (forall ((x U)) (not (P x))))))

provenance.source: authored from the S:logic-and-proof strand of the math-education concept graph; statement written here, not copied

prior_art.establishes: the proposition is valid; only OUR route fails to see it

notes: OPEN IN THIS LEDGER, NOT IN MATHEMATICS -- this is a standard first-order validity and the enum has no value for that distinction (see the lane diary). The reason it carries no evidence: axeyum returns `unknown` on it. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-quantifier-negation-duality.smt2`, which printed `; evidence kind=unknown certified=0 recheck=na arena=na ms=18` and then `unknown`. z3 on the identical file returns `unsat` in milliseconds, so the gap is ours and it is a small one: the negated form is a purely propositional combination of four quantified atoms over an uninterpreted sort, needing no instantiation heuristic at all, only the ability to treat a quantified subformula as a Boolean atom and then relate `forall x . phi` to `not exists x . not phi` by a skolem-free structural rule. This is the single most actionable entry in this batch: it is squarely inside the fragment axeyum advertises, it is the quantifier analogue of the already-proved F:de-morgan-laws, and closing it would flip this fact to `proved` with a real certificate.
